I think you're overreacting, dude. Seriously, I get that you're hurt...and I think that emotional pain itself is part of what's driving such a severe reaction from you. First, let me acknowledge a few things, though. Was he wrong to take your car? Was he wrong to drive drunk? Of course, and I'm not going to debate that, at all.

Now look at this from another angle. You've seen this guy as fit enough to dedicate 2/3's of your life to being his friend. That kind of friendship is not cheap. As far as "betrayal" goes, he could have done much, much, SO MUCH worse, if he had had malicious intentions. (I should know. The man I considered to be my brother-from-another-mother of a similar timeframe decided to lay his own legal charges on me, and force me to take the rap for it, then ducked out and abandoned me to the wolves. And I hadn't even done anything wrong, in the first place, other than assume he was a man of integrity.) Also, 20 drinks, as a minimum? It's highly possible he blacked out when he took the car, and that's why he doesn't remember taking it out. Even you admit you had to ask your girlfriend if you were in bed all last night, which tells me you are safeguarding and checking against having acted similarly.

My $0.02? Let things simmer down a bit, then sit your bro down, and tell him calmly, "Dude, I have a receipt from a burger joint the night you said you didn't take my car out, with your name on it. Tell me what really happened that night, because what you're telling me, and what the evidence says, aren't adding up." Get his side of the story, and figure out how to proceed from there. Right now, you're angry, and that anger and pain are blinding your reason and logic.

Point remains, as far as 'betrayals' go, this is pretty mild. And that's coming from someone who was, quite literally, betrayed by his best friend, and tossed to the wolves of the legal system.

A friend doesn't cut off a friend of twenty years after one blackout mistake. You really sound emotional right now, and that's understandable. In twenty years, this may be one of those stupid stories you guys joke about together.
